LGIU KNOWLEDGE EXCHANGE VISIT 
 
Galway County Council, in partnership with Galway City Council, hosted a very successful 
LGIU Chief Executive Knowledge Exchange from 8–10 April 2026. The event brought 
together Chief Executives from local authorities across Ireland, Northern Ireland, Scotland 
and England, providing a valuable forum for peer learning and strategic discussion. The 
programme focused on shared local government priorities, including economic 
development, climate action, renewable energy, sustainable tourism, urban and rural 
regeneration, and cross-border collaboration, while also strengthening professional 
relationships across jurisdictions. 
A key element of the visit was a site visit to Inis Mór in the Aran Islands, which showcased 
place-based and community-led approaches to development in an island context. The visit 
included engagement with Comharchumann Forbartha Árann Teo, presentations on climate 
action and community energy initiatives, and a guided visit to Dún Aonghasa. This element 
of the programme provided practical insights into delivering policy objectives in rural and 
island settings while highlighting the cultural, heritage and tourism assets of the Aran 
Islands.

BUILDING LIAISON OFFICER INITIATIVE 
  
On March 23rd, the Facilities team launched a new 
Building Liaison Officers initiative. 
  
Galway County Council as an organisation, has a very 
diverse property portfolio of around 60 buildings. 
  
We depend on our people to ensure each space remains 
safe, functional, welcoming, and aligned with the needs 
of staff, visitors, and stakeholders. Our new Building 
Liaison Officer initiative will be central to this — each 
Officer being the eyes and ears of their respective 
building. 
  
Some of the responsibilities are activities many of these persons already carry out naturally, 
including: 
• Maintaining tidy and well‑organised work areas in their respective building of work 
• Reporting operational or maintenance issues 
• Facilitating access for contractors and staff 
• Supporting a positive safety culture 
• Assisting with fire & emergency procedures including fire drill 
• Ensuring that the AED and First Aid equipment within the building is checked in 
accordance with our Health & Safety Management System. 
• Encouraging staff to train as fire wardens and first aiders in an effort to ensure there 
are first aiders and fire wardens present in the office 
• Directing any day-to-day operational issues to the Facilities section via., the new 
Facilities Register located on the Galway County Council intranet portal.

6 
 
This initiative aims to bring greater clarity, consistency, and recognition to this work already 
being done or to be done, effective March 23rd by those who are newly appointed Officers.  
Our Facilities team will support our Building Liaison Officers to 
ensure they feel confident in this role. 
  
This initiative was formally approved by our Chief Executive and 
Directors of Services at the end of 2025 and marks an important 
step forward in how we care for our buildings and the people 
who use them. 
  
The role of the Building Liaison Officers will support our 
organisational objectives and make a positive difference - 
building by building. 
OFFICE ACCOMMODATION PROJECT UPDATE 
  
The Office Accommodation Project continues to progress as a strategic priority for Galway 
County Council, aimed at consolidating staff currently dispersed across multiple leased sites 
into a single, modern, energy‑efficient headquarters at County Hall.  
  
Business continuity, service quality and staff well‑being remain central to planning as the 
Council prepares for a complex, multi‑year construction and transition period, with the build 
expected to commence in 2028. 
  
Staff engagement is a core component of the project. A dedicated Staff Working Group has 
been established to ensure two‑way communication, support staff input into building 
design, and help maintain service standards throughout all phases of transition. Town hall 
sessions for all staff will be held later in 2026, and union engagement is ongoing. 
  
An Independent Project Management and Quantity Surveying Consultant will be appointed 
to the Office Accommodation Project.  
  
In addition, an Integrated Design Team will be engaged to support the delivery of this 
project. Requests for Tenders have been published on the e‑Tenders platform, with a tender 
response date of March 30th 2026 with all appointments expected to be finalised by the end 
of Q 2 2026.  
  
Future considerations—including customer service improvements, elected member 
facilities, canteen capacity, sustainability, and transport planning— will be actively explored 
as part of the overall redesign. 
The Council remains committed to transparency and regular updates as this 
transformational project moves forward.

OPEN CALL FOR THE COMMUNITY SERVICE PROGRAMME 
Minister of State with responsibility for Community Development and Charities, Jerry 
Buttimer TD announced an Open Call for Applications under the Community Services 
Programme (CSP). The CSP Programme currently supports over 420 community-based 
organisations. 
The overarching vision of the CSP Programme is to support community organisations that 
operate to deliver a social purpose, to offer services that meet identified needs and provide 
employment locally contributing to sustainable, inclusive and empowered communities.  
Fulfilling a commitment made in the Programme for Government, this successful 
programme is now being opened to new entrants.  It will provide community-based 
organisations with an opportunity to access funding to support the employment of staff, in 
line with the programme’s objectives and principles.  
Pobal will provide support to organisations interested in making a preliminary application to 
join the CSP Programme from today until the closing date for applications on 8th May 2026. 
Following submission of a preliminary application that meets all eligible criteria, shortlisted 
applicants will then be invited to submit a full application to Pobal by 28th August 2026.  
Information Events will be held for successful applicants applying for the programme on the 
week beginning 27th July 2026. This will ensure those applying to the CSP Programme are 
fully equipped with the information that they need to apply for this funding. Details will be 
shared on the Pobal CSP webpage and on the Department of Rural and Community 
Development and the Gaeltacht’s website and social media channels.

THE WOMEN’S HEALTH PROGRAM 
The Empowering Women’s Health Programme, 
delivered in Spring 2026, has been a positive success, 
providing evidence-based information and practical 
support to women navigating perimenopause, 
menopause, and post-menopause. Hosted in twently 
locations across Galway county and also  livestreamed 
to the offshore islands, the three-week series offered 
free workshops led by a multidisciplinary team of 
specialists.  
 
 
 
Sessions included sleep hygiene and healthy 
ageing, yoga for resilience, mind–body 
connection, physiotherapy-led pelvic health, 
exercise therapy, breathwork, women’s 
health education from a Consultant OBGYN, 
resistance training guidance, and clinical 
nutrition for midlife wellbeing. Participation 
remained high throughout, with consistent in-
person engagement.

12 
 
 Feedback highlighted the value of accessible, 
expert-led information and the strong sense of 
community created throughout the programme. 
The initiative represents an effective collaboration 
between Healthy Galway, the HSE, Solas Family

UNDERSTAND TOGETHER CAMPAIGN – CLIFDEN AWARENESS EVENT 
 In conjunction with the Dementia Café initiative in Connemara, an Understand Together 
campaign event will be hosted in Clifden on 
Monday, 28 April, from 11:00am to 1:00pm, to 
raise awareness of dementia. The event aims to 
support people living with dementia, their 
families, and the wider community by increasing 
understanding and awareness across 
Connemara. 
The session is delivered in partnership with the Alzheimer Society of Ireland (ASI), Age 
Friendly, Forum Connemara CLG, the HSE, and the Healthy Galway Programme. 
Representatives for dementia awareness will be available on the day to share information, 
answer questions, and signpost attendees to local dementia supports and community 
resources. 
Participants will have the opportunity to learn about local Memory Cafés, activity 
programmes, health and training supports, and practical ways to create a more dementia-
inclusive community. The event will also offer guidance for carers and community members, 
as well as for local businesses and groups wishing to become more supportive and 
accessible. 
This Clifden event forms part of a wider commitment to reducing stigma, improving 
understanding, and strengthening community inclusion for people living with dementia 
across County Galway.

The Memory Café initiative continues to strengthen community-based support for people

TINY MUTINY 2026 
Tiny Muting, a creative call to Galway’s young artists is now open. Award-winning 
programme returns, inviting teenagers to develop and showcase original creative work. 
Now in its third year, Galway County Council Arts Office, in partnership with Sparkcatchers! 
has launched Tiny Mutiny 2026, an artist development programme for young people. 
Tiny Mutiny gives teenagers across County Galway the chance to create their own work 
from the ground up. Selected participants will receive mentorship from professional artists, 
a production budget, and practical support to bring their ideas to life over the summer. 
The programme welcomes all art forms. Previous projects have included music, animation, 
writing, graffiti, illustration, manga, film, dance and stop-motion- with an emphasis on 
creativity, experimentation and personal expression. 
Applications are now open to young people aged 13-17 living in County Galway. Participants 
will receive mentorship from a professional artist, financial support for materials, travel and 
production, ongoing guidance from Sparkcatchers! and a public platform to present their 
work. 
This year’s participants will showcase their completed 
work at The Mall Theatre, Tuam, on Friday, 18 
September 2026 as part of Culture Night. 
Last year’s participants described the programme as 
“inspiring”, “eye-opening” and “a once-in-a-lifetime 
opportunity”, highlighting the confidence gained and 
the experience of sharing their work with an audience. 
Tiny Mutiny continues to support young artists in 
developing their ideas and connecting with their 
communities through creativity.

The Creative Places Tuam Team recently had the pleasure of visiting Creative Places

the national network of 19 Creative Places and the role of Creative Places funding in 
creating a vibrant hub for artistic engagement, community-led cultural development and 
leaders in creative placemaking.

We are delighted to continue our support of theatre artists based in Galway County in 
partnership with Galway Theatre Festival again this year. The Arts Office is directly 
supporting CUISLE and 4 shows by Galway County theatre artists in this year’s Galway 
Theatre Festival programme. 
CUISLE is a year-round artist development programme supporting Galway-based theatre 
makers to develop new work and strengthen the independent theatre ecology of the West 
of Ireland. Two bursaries for Galway County artists have been awarded so far this year: 
Lorraine Stack – NASC, a heartwarming Irish language drama for young audiences.

From late April, Galway Public Libraries will offer a new Radon Monitor Loan

proactive health measures.

leading cause of lung cancer in Ireland after smoking. Through the scheme, library users can 
borrow a digital radon monitor just like a book, gaining a snapshot of radon levels in their 
homes. While not a replacement for the recommended three-month test, the monitors 
offer a valuable first step

The Croí Cónaithe Towns Fund supports the regeneration of towns, villages and cities by 
incentivising the reuse of vacant and underutilised residential and commercial buildings. The 
grants form a key component of national housing policy under Delivering Homes, Building 
Communities 2025–2030. 
The following grants are now available to individual vacant property owners: 
The Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant (VPRG) provides financial support to individuals 
to refurbish vacant residential properties or former commercial/public use buildings for use 
as homes. Grant support of up to €50,000 is available, with a further top‑up of up to 
€20,000 where a property is confirmed as derelict, subject to scheme conditions. 
From 31 March 2026, the VPRG has been enhanced for former commercial or public use 
buildings being converted in their entirety into two or more residential units. Additional 
top‑up funding is available in such cases, reflecting the scale and complexity of these 
conversions, while maintaining a single‑grant‑per‑building approach.

The Vacant Above the Shop Grant supports the conversion or refurbishment of long‑term 
vacant space above ground‑floor commercial premises where the commercial use is 
retained. Grant support of up to €135,000 is available, depending on the number of 
residential units created, and applies to both principal private residences and private rental 
accommodation, subject to a 10‑year clawback period. 
The Expert Advice Grant is a pre‑development support measure providing up to €5,000 to 
property owners considering either a Vacant Above the Shop conversion or the conversion 
of a former commercial/public use building into multiple residential units. The grant funds 
professional feasibility and advisory input and may be accessed independently of a 
subsequent capital grant application.

1. Purpose of Report 
The purpose of this report is to update Elected Members on the current profile of social 
housing demand in County Galway, based on the Approved Housing List, with specific 
regard to: 
• Area of Choice 
• Household size requirements 
• Basis of Need 
• Age profile 
In presenting this analysis, 1‑bed and 2‑bed demand is considered jointly, reflecting both 
the operation of the Allocation Scheme, which allows for 1‑bed households to be 
accommodated in 2‑bed dwellings, and the prevailing supply profile, which is weighted 
towards 2‑bed units. 
2. Overall Level of Demand (Combined 1‑ & 2‑Bed Analysis) 
As at the date of this report, there are 2,999 approved households on the social housing 
list. 
When 1‑bed and 2‑bed demand is considered together: 
• 1‑ & 2‑bed households combined: 1,735 households (58%) 
• 3‑bed households: 1,068 households (36%) 
• 4‑bed and larger households (4–6 bed): 196 households (6%) 
This combined analysis demonstrates that almost three‑fifths of all approved households 
can be accommodated within the 1‑ and 2‑bed stock, aligning closely with the typical 
output of current and planned housing delivery programmes. 
3. Demand by Area of Choice (1‑ & 2‑Bed Combined) 
Across all Areas of Choice, combined 1‑ and 2‑bed demand represents the dominant 
housing need, with particularly high concentrations in the following locations:

67 
 
• Athenry and Environs 
• Oranmore / Baile Chlair 
• Tuam 
• Loughrea and Environs 
These growth areas display both: 
• High absolute demand, and 
• A demand profile well matched to 2‑bed delivery, supporting efficient allocations 
where 1‑bed households are housed in 2‑bed units in accordance with the Allocation 
Scheme. 
In more rural and Connemara areas, while overall volumes are lower, the relative 
proportion of 1‑ and 2‑bed demand remains high, reinforcing the countywide relevance of 
this combined category. 
4. Basis of Need – Implications for Unit Size 
Assessment by Basis of Need further supports the combined 1‑ and 2‑bed approach. 
The largest single category of approved households is: 
• Households requiring Rent Supplement to access private rented accommodation 
(1,546 households) 
This cohort is predominantly comprised of single-person and smaller households, for whom 
1‑ or 2‑bed accommodation is appropriate. 
Similarly, significant demand arises from households with: 
• Disability-related housing needs 
• Medical or compassionate grounds 
• Homeless or emergency accommodation backgrounds 
These categories typically require smaller, well-designed, and accessible units, again 
reinforcing the operational suitability of 2‑bed units accommodating both 1‑bed and 2‑bed 
approved households. 
5. Demand by Age Profile 
Age profile analysis further supports the combined approach: 
• The largest demand cohorts fall within the 28–47 age range, typically single adults or 
smaller family units. 
• A substantial cohort of older persons (65+) is also present, the majority of whom are 
approved for 1‑bed accommodation, but can be appropriately housed in 2‑bed 
units, particularly where design and accessibility standards are met. 
This provides flexibility in allocations while supporting ageing-in-place and future-proofed 
housing stock.

68 
 
6. Key Observations for Members 
• 1‑ and 2‑bed households account for the majority of housing demand in County 
Galway when considered in line with allocation policy. 
• The current pipeline supply profile, which is predominantly 2‑bed and 3-bed, is 
broadly aligned with demand when allocations flexibility is applied. 
• Treating 1‑ and 2‑bed demand together provides a more realistic and operationally 
accurate picture of housing need and supply alignment. 
• Continued emphasis on 3‑bed delivery remains necessary, but should be viewed 
alongside the clear predominance of smaller household demand. 
 
7. Conclusion 
When assessed in accordance with the Allocation Scheme and prevailing supply 
characteristics, the Approved Housing List demonstrates that the majority of social housing 
demand in County Galway can be met through 2‑bed provision, accommodating both 
1‑bed and 2‑bed approved households. 
This combined approach supports: 
• More efficient use of stock 
• Improved alignment between demand and delivery 
• Greater flexibility in allocations 
• Stronger evidence-based planning and funding submissions 
The Housing Authority will continue to monitor demand trends and report to Members 
through regular Chief Executive’s Reports and Housing SPC updates.

Galway County Council, Galway City Council and Transport Infrastructure Ireland welcome 
the decision of An Coimisiún Pleanála to grant approval for the N6 Galway City Ring Road.

delivery of a more sustainable, integrated and efficient transport network for Galway.

will improve connectivity to the national road network, reduce unnecessary strategic traffic 
within the city centre and create greater opportunity to reallocate road space for walking, 
cycling, public transport and placemaking. In doing so, it will support improved road safety, 
quality of life, climate objectives and economic development.

planning process has been very difficult for the home and property owners affected by the 
proposed route.

COUNTY GALWAY ORAL HERITAGE PROJECT 
Funding has been awarded by The Heritage Council to support the delivery of the County 
Galway Oral Heritage Project, which represents the first implementation phase of the

collaborations, and a County‑wide public event during National Heritage Week 2026.

resources, will enable the translation of strategic recommendations into practical actions, 
ensuring that Galway’s rich oral heritage is preserved, accessible, and embedded as a living 
community resource for future generations.
